target.title: fix: DashScope and Moonshot endpoints misclassified as custom when the provider plugin is not installed
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where DashScope/Qwen, Moonshot, Z.AI, DeepSeek, Groq, Cerebras, and Chutes base URLs were misclassified as `custom` endpoints whenever the owning provider plugin was not installed. These provider plugins are externalized (excluded from dist packaging), so installed gateways had no source for their endpoint classes: DashScope image-describe prompts were moved out of user content (breaking vision requests), and streaming-usage / developer-role compat defaults regressed for anyone pointing a generic provider key at these endpoints.

The same root cause made `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts` ("places DashScope image prompts in user content before images") and the DashScope/Qwen cases in `src/agents/model-compat.test.ts` fail deterministically in any source checkout where `pnpm build` had run (bundled discovery prefers `dist/extensions` once it exists, and the built tree does not contain externalized plugins). This silently wedged local `scripts/pr` landing lanes, which run build → check → test in one worktree; two lanes looped on it for hours on 2026-07-04.

## Why This Change Was Made

Endpoint classification is endpoint-keyed request policy — the code contract in `resolveProviderRequestCapabilities` explicitly says users can point a generic provider key at Moonshot or DashScope and still need native request policy. That contract broke when these plugins were externalized, because classification metadata only lived in plugin manifests. The official external provider catalog (`scripts/lib/official-external-provider-catalog.json`) is the core-shipped registry for exactly these plugins, so it now mirrors each plugin's manifest `providerEndpoints`, and `provider-attribution` appends catalog metadata after installed/bundled manifests (first match wins, so installed manifests stay authoritative).

Boundaries: classification reads the repo-bundled catalog JSON only — hosted marketplace feeds can never influence endpoint classification (it is SSRF/attribution policy surface). Endpoint classes core does not recognize (`deepinfra-native`, `gmi-native`, `qwen-portal-native`) are mirrored faithfully but stay inert via the existing allowlist filter, identical to installed-manifest behavior; widening the core class union is a separate product decision. `providerRequest` (provider-id-keyed metadata) is intentionally not mirrored: running a canonical provider id without its plugin is not a supported configuration.

Alternatives rejected: preferring the source `extensions/` tree in built checkouts would fight deliberate, test-pinned bundled-dir behavior and leave shipped dist gateways broken; mocking the failing tests would hide a real shipped regression.

## User Impact

Installed (dist) gateways classify DashScope, Moonshot, Z.AI, DeepSeek, Groq, Cerebras, and Chutes endpoints natively again without requiring the provider plugin: DashScope image description places prompts in user content, and streaming-usage / developer-role compat defaults apply by URL as documented. Local `pnpm build && pnpm test` is deterministic again in source checkouts, unwedging `scripts/pr` landing lanes. Installing a provider plugin still overrides catalog metadata.

## Evidence

- Repro fixed: `pnpm build && pnpm test src/media-understanding/image.test.ts src/agents/model-compat.test.ts` — previously 1 deterministic failure in image.test.ts plus DashScope/Qwen model-compat failures with a dist tree present; now green (29/29 image incl. the DashScope case, 104/104 agents shard, 54/54 plugins shard), and the same set is green pre-build.
- Negative control: reverting only the provider-attribution catalog merge (dist present) reproduces exactly the reported failure (1 failed / 28 passed in image.test.ts); restoring it returns 29/29.
- Verified `dist/extensions` in a built checkout contains no `qwen`/`moonshot`, confirming the failing state under test.
- New regression tests: `src/agents/provider-attribution.catalog-endpoints.test.ts` simulates a dist tree (no ambient manifests) and pins classification, manifest-over-catalog precedence, and unknown-class inertness; `src/plugins/official-external-provider-endpoints.test.ts` enforces the catalog↔manifest mirror for every dist-excluded plugin that declares `providerEndpoints` (parses the package.json dist excludes), which would have caught the original externalization regression.
- `tsgo` core + core-test lanes green; oxlint clean; Codex structured review (gpt-5.5) clean after addressing one finding about the intentionally-inert mirrored classes (now documented in code and pinned by tests).
